title: ～つもりで — “with the intention of ～ / as if ～”
summary: Shows the intention or mindset with which someone does an action. It attaches to a verb dictionary form or noun + の, and the main clause says what they do with that intention. It can also mean “acting as if ～ (is the case)”.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形＋つもりで＋行動

patterns.gloss: treating it as ～; as if it were ～

body.p: Verb dictionary form + つもりで explains the mindset behind what follows: 留学するつもりで、お金を貯めている. The main clause is usually an ongoing or repeated action.
With nouns, 初心者のつもりで or 客のつもりで means “thinking of yourself as ～”. It is often used for advice such as 最後だと思うつもりで頑張る, asking someone to take a certain attitude.

body.h: Not the same as つもりだ
body.p: ～つもりだ ends a sentence as a plan (留学するつもりだ). ～つもりで connects to another clause and shows the purpose or mindset behind the main action.

examples.ja: 留学（りゅうがく）するつもりで、お金（かね）を貯（た）めている。
examples.romaji: Ryuugaku suru tsumori de, okane o tamete iru.
examples.tr: I’m saving money with the intention of studying abroad.
examples.note: The goal comes first, then the action done for it.

examples.ja: 新（あたら）しい店（みせ）を開（ひら）くつもりで、資金（しきん）を集（あつ）めている。
examples.romaji: Atarashii mise o hiraku tsumori de, shikin o atsumete iru.
examples.tr: I’m gathering funds with the intention of opening a new shop.

examples.ja: プロになるつもりで、毎日（まいにち）練習（れんしゅう）を続（つづ）けている。
examples.romaji: Puro ni naru tsumori de, mainichi renshuu o tsudzukete iru.
examples.tr: I keep practicing every day with the intention of becoming a professional.

pitfalls: The verb before つもりで must be in the dictionary form (or ない-form), not the masu-form: 行くつもりで, not 行きますつもりで.
Do not confuse it with つもりだ at sentence end. つもりで needs a following clause.
